feed.title: Getting BIP54 past the finish line

entry.title: Getting BIP54 past the finish line
entry.summary:
The discussion surrounding BIP 54, from a personal viewpoint, highlights several critical aspects of its development and the ongoing efforts to reach consensus within the Bitcoin development community. Initially reintroduced by Poinsot at the close of 2023 and into early 2024, BIP 54 aims to address prominent security vulnerabilities in the Bitcoin protocol. These issues include the timewarp attack, lengthy block validation times for pre-SegWit scripts, merkle tree malleability with 64-byte transactions, and potential duplicate coinbase transactions.
Throughout various design discussions, there has been a significant focus on resolving these concerns, with particular attention paid to advanced attack variants like the Murch-Zawy scenario. By early 2025, a draft BIP was proposed, leading to extensive debates particularly regarding the rule to eliminate 64-byte transactions which some developers opposed vigorously. Following these discussions, a reference implementation complete with test vectors was put forward at the end of 2025, addressing broader technical concerns including the encoding methods in coinbase transaction nlocktimes.
Further public demonstrations, notably on signet, have showcased the severity of long block validation times, prompting additional conversations especially concerning 64-byte transactions. A pull request to implement BIP 54 in Bitcoin Core is currently under review and testing, alongside parallel efforts in btcd to ensure inter-compatibility between implementations.
It's suggested that moving BIP 54 towards activation requires not only resolving these technical disputes but also comprehensive reviews and testing of the reference implementation to uphold high technical standards. This includes further real-life testing on vulnerabilities as previously conducted on signet. The community is encouraged to contribute their analysis and viewpoints to foster a robust review process, akin to the standards set during previous protocol upgrades such as Schnorr/Taproot.
Looking ahead, it’s deemed realistic to consider activating BIP 54 around the second semester of 2027, contingent upon achieving community consensus and barring any unforeseen disruptions. There's an acknowledgment that other future consensus changes, possibly in response to post-quantum threats or other security enhancements, should not be overlooked by the community. Engaging in these discussions and preparatory work is crucial for the continued evolution and security of Bitcoin’s protocol framework.
